transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

I cannot tell you which part to buy yet because 'not draining' has two very different causes that require opposite fixes: a blockage in the hose/waste pipe, or a failed drain pump. Replacing the wrong part will not fix it. The next step is to listen to what the machine does when it tries to empty. Please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin' programme and stand near the bottom front of the machine while it starts to drain. Does it make a humming/buzzing noise (the pump trying to push water out), or is it completely silent?
It hums but the water doesn't move, there's a loud hum and a little rattle. So is it the pump then?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. No, it is not most likely the pump yet. A humming noise with a rattle usually means the pump motor is trying to turn but something is physically stopping it—most commonly a coin, button, or hair grip jammed in the impeller (the fan blades inside). It could also be that the impeller itself has broken off and is rattling around. Because I cannot confirm the exact internal layout for your specific FD 9409 model, and because accessing the pump usually requires removing the back panel or tilting the machine to reach the sump hose, this is not a simple owner swap. If you are confident in using tools, you could try to remove the filter housing again and check if anything is stuck in the visible impeller, but do not force it. Given the rattle and the hum, the most likely outcome is that the pump needs replacing or clearing of debris by a professional. I would recommend calling an engineer to inspect and repair this safely.
